WHAT AM I LOOKING AT? · Membrane force N₁ / N₂
opened from the ? on the row, or from the legend on the canvas. Same text in the tab’s guide page.
N₁ compression (blue) · N₂ tension (red)
in the plane of the shell
m₁ / m₂ bend the slab across its own thickness
out of the plane of the shell
N₁ and N₂ are the two principal MEMBRANE forces: force per metre of width, in the
plane of the shell. They are what a shell carries load with. Blue is compression,
red is tension, and the pale middle of the ramp is a patch carrying almost nothing.
Read it like this. A well-shaped shell is mostly one colour — compression — with
tension only near free edges and openings. A red patch in the middle of a dome is
the shape fighting the load, and it is usually cheaper to change the shape than to
thicken the slab. Bending m₁ / m₂ tells the other half of that story: a shell in pure
membrane action has almost none, so wherever m is large the shell is acting as a
plate, and that is exactly where automatic thickening will add material.
Units follow the tab: kN/m here, kNm/m for moments, MPa for stress.
The scale is this model’s own peak unless you pin it — so two models are not
comparable by colour alone, and the legend always prints the numbers.
